commit de4c78411a917b80f4ec5e60015c4f350ac0be9f
Author: Igor Brandao <brandaodeveloperapp@gmail.com>
Date:   Sun Sep 6 18:54:57 2026 -0300

    security: kill RCE from data file, stop denoise eating real errors
    
    Red-team found three defects that a token saver must never have.
    
    CRITICAL: `verify:` frontmatter was piped to `/bin/sh -c`, so any markdown
    file under the memory dir was executable code. A planted memory ran its
    payload and reported a green check. Declared commands now run through
    execFile with a parsed argv, shell metacharacters are refused outright, and
    nothing executes at all without an explicit --run.
    
    Two algorithm defects made bilro hide the very output it exists to surface.
    A deterministic failure present in every run crossed the df ceiling and was
    dropped forever; and a failure whose text carries a pid, ip or uuid took the
    volatile branch, which skipped the never-seen-before guard, so even a brand
    new error vanished. Both are fixed by a severity floor: a line reporting a
    failure is never noise, however often it repeats, and it outranks everything
    when output is trimmed to a budget.
    
    One test asserted the second bug rather than catching it, using a failure
    line as its example of a droppable one. Fixture corrected.
    
    Also: observe() writes in one transaction and caps input lines, sqlite opens
    with busy_timeout and WAL, subprocesses carry a timeout, and the ledger
    writes atomically via rename.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01WYr99D31EZn3cW2792yZAM

diff --git a/lib/exec.js b/lib/exec.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..c730365
--- /dev/null
+++ b/lib/exec.js
@@ -0,0 +1,37 @@
+import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
+
+const SHELL_META = /[;&|`$><\n\r\\]|\$\(|\|\||&&/;
+
+/** Splits a command line into argv, honouring quotes. No shell involved. */
+export function toArgv(line) {
+  const out = [];
+  const re = /"([^"]*)"|'([^']*)'|(\S+)/g;
+  let m;
+  while ((m = re.exec(line))) out.push(m[1] ?? m[2] ?? m[3]);
+  return out;
+}
+
+export function isSafe(line) {
+  return !SHELL_META.test(line);
+}
+
+/**
+ * Runs a declared command with no shell, so a value read from a data file
+ * cannot chain, redirect or substitute its way into something else.
+ */
+export function runDeclared(line, { timeout = 30000, cwd } = {}) {
+  if (!isSafe(line)) return { ok: false, refused: true, output: "usa sintaxe de shell" };
+  const argv = toArgv(line);
+  if (!argv.length) return { ok: false, refused: true, output: "vazio" };
+  try {
+    const output = execFileSync(argv[0], argv.slice(1), {
+      encoding: "utf8",
+      timeout,
+      cwd,
+      maxBuffer: 8 * 1024 * 1024,
+    });
+    return { ok: true, refused: false, output };
+  } catch (e) {
+    return { ok: false, refused: false, output: String(e.stdout || e.message || e).slice(0, 200) };
+  }
+}

+const MAX_LINES = 20000;
+
+/**
+ * A line that reports a failure is never noise, however often it repeats. A
+ * build that breaks the same way every day is still the answer to "what
+ * happened", and the whole point of the tool is lost if it hides it.
+ */
+const SEVERE = /\b(error|erro|failed|failing|failure|falhou|fatal|panic|exception|traceback|refused|denied|unauthorized|forbidden|timeout|timed out|cannot|could not|no such|not found|undefined is not|segmentation fault|✕|✗|FAIL)\b/i;
+
+export function isSevere(line) {
+  return SEVERE.test(line);
+}
+

   return command
